title: Tool-call schema failure classifier and repair playbook for streaming tool invocations
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Problem statement: When LLM-generated tool/function calls are delivered in streaming scenarios we observe a class of failures that are not well-covered by existing validation rules. These failures are often transient (partial JSON fragments, interleaved stream tokens, or KV cache mismatches) and produce opaque runtime errors that make remediation by callers and SREs difficult. This ticket defines a failure classifier, human-friendly error messages, and a repair playbook that runtime and SDK layers can adopt to improve debuggability and automated recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Define a short enumerated failure taxonomy (<=8 categories) that covers streaming-specific failure modes and maps to remediation actions.
Publish canonical user-facing error messages for each failure class, with suggested next steps for SDKs and server-side fallbacks.
Implement telemetry hooks that emit the failure code, model id, request context (stream vs non-stream), and a sample-safe diagnostic snapshot for at least two representative runtime paths.
Runtime implements a permissive fallback mode that attempts safe repair for
Document unit/integration tests and runbook for on-call SREs.
A small dogfood release where the runtime returns the new error codes for 10% of streaming tool calls in the staging environment.
technical_notes: Streaming-specific failure modes we observed in incidents: PARTIAL_JSON_STREAM (JSON truncated mid-object), TOKEN_SPLIT_KEY (tokenization split in the middle of a quoted key/value), INTERLEAVED_TOOL_OUTPUT (model interleaves plain text and tool call fragments), KV_CACHE_REVISION_MISMATCH (tool call parameters reference stale KV cache entries), COERCION_EDGECASE (value looks like correct type but fails strict JSON schema coercion).
Avoid adding nested schema objects in error metadata returned to callers — include only short tags and a canonical pointer to internal diagnostic blobs stored in internal object store (safe for PII).

Design principle: surface a single short machine-readable error_code and a concise human_message. Example: {error_code: "PARTIAL_JSON_STREAM", human_message: "Tool call payload truncated during streaming — ask the model to re-emit the final JSON object or enable post-stream reassembly via SDK."}. (Runtime will return fields in top-level envelope; SDKs may map to richer diagnostics.)
Because date constraints: updated_at >= created_at; ensure telemetry uses ISO-8601 timestamps and request ids consistent with existing tracing conventions.

Prioritize non-breaking runtime behavior: default runtime behavior remains strict; introduce a per-customer and per-route permissive_repair setting that enables automated heuristics (reassembly, forgiving coercion).
implementation_steps: 1) Draft failure taxonomy and canonical error messages (this doc).
2) Add enums to runtime error contract and update API schema documentation.
3) Implement lightweight stream reassembly module: buffer up to 512 bytes of trailing stream tokens and attempt to close truncated JSON objects using heuristics (balance braces, close open strings).
4) Implement safe coercion layer: for numeric fields accept quoted-numeric strings when permissive_repair is enabled; log coercion as telemetry event.
5) Add feature flag + per-route config to enable permissive_repair in dedicated/private and toggle in hosted for pilot customers.
6) Update SDKs (JS, Python): surface error_code and provide helper helpers: .retry_as_reassembled() and .request_tool_reemit_prompt().
7) Write unit tests for each failure class and integration tests that simulate partial stream fragments and token-split keys.
8) Add on-call runbook and a dashboard showing frequency by error_code, affected model, and route.
9) Dogfood for 2 weeks, collect metrics, and iterate on messages/heuristics.
10) Ship to production with rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
testing_plan: Unit tests for reassembly heuristics with corpus of 200 truncated examples (JSON structures, nested arrays, strings with escapes).
Integration tests that run streaming sessions against the runtime and assert the error_code is returned for malformed fragments and that permissive_repair returns corrected payloads where safe.
Fuzzing harness that injects token-split events mid-key and validates that coercion never silently changes semantic types when strict mode is enabled.
Canary runs in staging with telemetry collection: ensure false-positive repair rate < 0.5% and regression in latency < 6ms p50.
Manual SRE playthrough using the runbook to confirm readable incident handling steps.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit sample-safe diagnostic blob id and link in traces: traces include diagnostic_blob_id not raw payloads.
Track repair_success_rate when permissive_repair is enabled.
Alert: error_code PARTIAL_JSON_STREAM > 1000/day or repair_success_rate < 80% triggers SEV-2 investigation.
Dashboard: stacked bar of error_code by model and by route, with latency overlay to detect repair-induced regressions.
rollout_and_migration: Phase 0: Publish spec and SDK helpers (this sprint).
Phase 1: Dogfood with internal teams and staging 10% traffic for two weeks.
Phase 2: Expand to selected pilot customers; collect UX feedback from SDK users on message clarity.
Phase 3: Default permissive_repair off; GA of error codes and docs. Customers can enable via per-route config or tenant flag.
Migration note: older SDK versions that do not understand new error_code should map unknown errors to 'Tool call failed — see runtime docs'. Ensure backward compatibility tests pass.

example_error_messages: PARTIAL_JSON_STREAM: 'Tool call JSON payload truncated during streaming. Ask the model to re-emit or enable post-stream reassembly via SDK helper. If you are the integrator, retry the request once with idempotent inputs.'

TOKEN_SPLIT_KEY: 'Tool call contained a key/value split across token boundaries — consider increasing model temperature or using deterministic decoding. SDK can attempt to reassemble if permissive_repair is enabled.'
COERCION_FAILED: 'Tool call parameter "timeout_ms" expected integer but received "30s". Enable permissive_coercion or correct call schema. See docs for safe coercion rules.'
KV_CACHE_REVISION_MISMATCH: 'Tool call referenced state that has changed since generation (kv cache revision mismatch). Retry after fetching latest state or pin kv_revision to the call.'
INTERLEAVED_TOOL_OUTPUT: 'Tool-call fragments were interleaved with free-form text. Use structured function-calling mode or configure the model to output a single structured envelope.'
